articleTitle: Integral representation of solutions of the wave equation based on Poincaré wavelets
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: We present here an exact integral representation of solutions of the wave equation with constant coefficients in two spatial dimensions in terms of localized solutions. A solution is given as a superposition of localized solutions each of which lives in the reference system, which moves in the x direction with velocity v. To obtain any solution, we must take into account all |v| ≤ c, where c is the velocity of wave propagation, and use also shifts and scaling. The representation is constructed by means of space-temporal wavelet theory which is applied to the section of a solution in the plane y = 0.

articleTitle: A new approach to solution of generalized (3+1)-dimensional sine-Gordon equation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: The new exact solutions of the three-dimensional sine-Gordon (SG) equation are obtained. These solutions depend on arbitrary function F(α), which argument is some function α(x, y, z, t). The ansatz α is found from the linear equation with respect to x, y, z, t, which coefficients are arbitrary functions depending on α. These coefficients must satisfy a system of algebraic equations. The classical and generalized SG-equations with first derivatives with respect to x, y, z, t are solved by this method. The SG-equation with only first time derivative is considered separately. The approaches for the solutions of SG-equation with variable amplitude are proposed. These methods admit natural generalization in case of integration of the abovementioned types of equations in a space with any number of dimensions.

articleTitle: Solution of diffraction problems by null field and T-matrix methods with accounting for wave field analytical continuation singularities
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: It is shown that the correct reduction of the null field identity to integral equation requires that the surface, on which null field condition is satisfied, covers the set of singularities of diffraction field analytical continuation into interior of the scatterer. Moreover, the solution algorithm of the obtained integral equation is demonstrated to be fastest and most stable, if the above mentioned surface is constructed by analytical deformation of scatterer boundary.

articleTitle: Electrodynamic characteristics of a strip antenna in a resonant anisotropic medium
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: A study is made of the current distribution and input impedance of a perfectly conducting straight strip antenna immersed in a homogeneous anisotropic medium such as a magnetized plasma. It is assumed that the antenna is perpendicular to the direction of an external static magnetic field. Integral equations for the antenna current are obtained. On the basis of their solution, approximate expressions for the current distribution and input impedance of a sufficiently narrow strip antenna are derived. The expressions are given in the form suitable for numerical computations which are performed for the practically important case of a magnetized plasma modeled upon the Earth's ionosphere.

articleTitle: Damage hazard prediction while drilling
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: We consider the new method of damage hazard precursor of the bit drill approaching the fracture while the borehole drilling. We used three suppositions for our suggesting: a) the theory of weak boundary existing inside solid Earth, b) the unusual S* arising when the pressure center source approaches the boundary and c) the bit drill using as a source. All above mentioned facts have corresponding confirmations on the practice.

articleTitle: Light scattering problem solutions using the field expansions in wave functions: convergence and the Rayleigh hypothesis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: The problem of light scattering by a non-spherical obstacle is most often solved today by the SVM, EBCM and PMM methods applying the field expansions in terms of wave functions. The methods are based on quite different formulations of the problem and hence were earlier discussed separately. We demonstrate tight relations of the methods and present some results of our recent theoretical and numerical studies of the methods that illustrate their similarity and differences.

articleTitle: The Riemann problem for the stochastically perturbed non-viscous Burgers equation and the pressureless gas dynamics model
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: Proceeding from the method of stochastic perturbation of a Langevin system associated with the non-viscous Burgers equation we construct a solution to the Riemann problem for the non-interacting particles and sticky particles systems. We analyze the difference in the behavior of discontinuous solution for these two models and relations between them.

articleTitle: On applicability of the extended boundary condition method with the spheroidal basis
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: The problem of light scattering by small particles is commonly solved today by the extended boundary condition method (EBCM) that uses expansions of the fields in terms of wave functions. The method is known to have a limited range of applicability. We analytically study the method in the case when spheroidal functions are applied. We find the conditions under which such a version of the EBCM method is mathematically correct and can be used for calculations in the far-field zone.

articleTitle: General analytical treatment of the graded interfaces with negative-index nanocomposites
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: We investigate the electrodynamics of structures incorporating nanocomposites with negative dielectric permittivity and magnetic permeability, the popular “left-handed metamaterials”. We obtain analytical solutions to the Helmholtz equation for gradient-index interfaces between the positive and negative index part. We derive expressions for the field intensity as well as for the transmission- and reflection-coefficients, assuming that the graded region across the interface is smaller than the operating wavelength. We then compare the analytical results with the numerical results obtained by the Transfer Matrix Method (TMM). The model allows for arbitrary frequency dependencies and lossy media.

articleTitle: Andreev reflection and the semiclassical Bogoliuobov-De Gennes Hamiltonian
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: We present a semi-classical analysis of the opening of superchannels in gated mesoscopic SNS or SFS junctions. For perfect Josephson junctions (i.e. hardwall potential), this was considered by [2] in the framework of scattering matrices. Here we allow for imperfections in the junction, so that the complex order parameter continues as a smooth function, which is a constant in the superconducting banks, and vanishes rapidly inside the lead. The problem of finding quantization rules for Andreev states near energy E close to the Fermi level, reduces to finding the zeroes of the determinant of a monodromy matrix, which we characterize partially by means of geometric quantities.

articleTitle: Connection between representations of Heisenberg and su(1, 1) algebras
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: The expression of Hermite polynomials via Laguerre ones allows to connect the standard representations of the Heisenberg algebra with representations of generalized oscillator algebra, related to the Laguerre polynomials. We give the connection between the measures participating in the orthogonality relations for these polynomials and the connection between energy levels of related oscillators. Such considerations can be extended to a general case in which Hermite polynomials are replaced by polynomials orthogonal with respect to a symmetric measure.

articleTitle: Application of orthogonal wavelets for the stochastic wavelet-Galerkin solution of the Kraichnan-Orszag system
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: The estimation of statistical momenta of the stochastic systems dx/dt = f(x, {ξ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub>}<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub>), where {ξ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub>}<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</sub> is the set of random parameters, is an important problem in computations. The direct solution consists in integration of evolution equations followed by the Monte-Carlo averaging. Recently a method of estimation statistical momenta of such systems, the so-called intrusive method, based on the expansion x(ξ, t) = Σ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub> c<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>(t)Φ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>(ξ) was used to make the original system into Galerkin system of equations with known basic functions Φ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>(ξ). The most of the research was based on the polynomial basic functions Φ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sub>(ξ), that is why called a polynomial chaos expansion (R.Ghanem and P.Spanos, 1991). In our contribution we use the expansion with respect to the orthogonal wavelets, instead of orthogonal polynomials. Developing the ideas of Wiener-Haar expansion (Le Maitre et al., 2004), that uses wavelets for studying certain domains of the random parameters with better resolution than other, we construct an expansion using the set of the orthogonal Daubechies wavelets (DAUB4, DAUB6, ...) with compact support. Being sensitive to the derivatives higher than one, our expansion provides better possibilities for estimation of statistical momenta of random solutions of differential equations. An example of the Kraichnan-Orszag system (S.A.Orszag and L.R.Bissonnette, 1967) is presented.

articleTitle: The interaction of creeping waves on a smooth anisotropic impedance surface
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: Electromagnetic creeping waves running along a smooth convex anisotropic impedance surface are studied. The adiabatic expansion for creeping waves works if attenuations of modes do not coincide. The leading order term of the expansion may have the TE or TM polarization. We consider the case where the adiabatic approach fails near the points of coincidence of attenuation parameters of the modes with different polarizations. We assume that this coincidence takes place on a curve on the surface. We have found the asymptotic expansion which works near this curve. This expansion is matched with the adiabatic expansions, and the effect of the initiation of the new mode is described.

articleTitle: Adaptive finite element method based on superconvergence
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: The h-refinement algorithm based on superconvergence in the framework of the finite element method is presented. The algorithm is applied to the bound state calculations in the few-body quantum systems. The efficiency and accuracy of the approach is illustrated with the one-dimensional quadratic oscillator and with the neon trimer described by the three-dimensional Schrödinger equation.

articleTitle: Three qubit operation in the five level optical medium
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: Possible optical implementation of CCNOT gate based on the M-configuration system of atomic levels is discussed. The semiclassical estimations of summary conditional phase shift for the corresponding Controlled Phase Shift (CPS) operator are got. To this end the nonlinear optical phenomena (such as EIT) connected with resonant interaction of electromagnetic field acting on the four transients of five level atomic system with M-configuration (in stationary operating mode) is investigated. It is shown that the M-scheme may be used for implementation of CCNOT gate.

articleTitle: Modes of two-mirror cavity with non-coinciding main curvature directions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: For a linear cavity, restricted by mirrors with distinct main directions of curvature, we have researched stability conditions and obtained explicit analytical formulae for a principal term of a basic mode. When the principal term of the fundamental mode cannot be uniquely determined, we obtain formulae for sets of solutions in a main approximation. Operators, transforming basic mode to higher modes, are expressed in terms of eigenvectors of 2×2 matrix, whose eigenvalues are responsible for stability conditions of the cavity.

articleTitle: On features of Smith-Purcell radiation resonant regimes in relativistic diffraction generator
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: The relativistic diffraction generators (RDG) are classified among the most promising sources for generation of long-pulsed high power coherent microwave radiation in the centimeter and millimeter wavelengths range. The operation of this type of microwave generators is based on Smith-Purcell radiation phenomenon. The numerical studies of the multiwave mechanisms of interaction between tubular electron beam and fields of super-dimensional axisymmetric periodical slow-wave structures (SWS) of corrugated waveguide in relativistic diffraction generator in the frequency range of 2π-type oscillations are presented in this report.

articleTitle: Antiplane wave scattering on tunnel cylindrical cavities with fixed inclusions of radial cross-section in orthotropic body
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: It is presented numerical-analytical technique for solving longitudinal shear wave diffraction scattering on tunnel cylindrical cavities in anisotropic orthorhombic system elastic massif with fixed inclusions of radial cross-section problems. Proposed method is based on generalized metaharmonic equation integration in affinetransformed coordinates. Amplitude wave field characteristics are presented by series with undefined coefficients on basic particular solutions. These solutions are expressed through cylindrical functions of polar coordinate in affinetransformed areas. Considered edge problems are reduced to infinite linear algebraic system analysis by using the method of least squares. Results of numerical and qualitative analysis for constructed solutions and wave field characteristics studies, when problem parameters are varied, are presented.

articleTitle: Connections between seismology, waveguide physics and quantum mechanics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: It is well-known that surface waves represent usually the main part of seismograms because of the 2D-character of their propagation. Their interaction with lateral heterogeneities is important not only in seismology but also in non-destructive testing (NDT), solid state physics and other disciplines. If we consider an elastic half-space the differential operator from the Navier equation has an infinite domain of definition with the consequence of a mixed spectrum: the discrete part represented by surface waves and the continuous part represented by body waves. We can identify the surface waves with the bound states of an atom and the body waves with the unbound ones. Conceptions of quantum mecanics like Dirac's perturbation theory and others can be profitably used for the theory of disturbed wave-guides. We present a bra-ket formalism for the Rayleigh and Love waves and observe that contrary to the Love waves, which follow from a standard Sturm-Liouville problem, the eigenvalue problem for Rayleigh waves is a generalized and complicated one. The discrete eigenfunction system of the surface waves is incomplete and it is not yet proven wether the surface waves and body aves together build up a complete system. It is not easy to determine expansion coefficients within any expansion containing surface waves because of the mixed character of the governing operator's eigenspectrum. An approximation technique is proposed to determine the coefficients by minimizing a special functional F<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and the results are compared with an impedance jump problem, the only configuration with an exact solution for reflection and transmission coefficients for surface waves.

articleTitle: Diffraction of a plane wave with an amplitude linearly varying along its front on a rigid semi-infinite screen
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: We deal with a new non-stationary problem of diffraction. A plane wave with an amplitude linearly varying along the front is incident on a rigid semiinfinite screen. Exact analytical solution of the problem is obtained by the Smirnov-Sobolev method.

articleTitle: Application of circular harmonic wavelets towards solution of the Fredholm type integral equations
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: In our work we extend a new approach presented in towards solution of the Fredholm type integral equations of the second kind. The so-called circular or periodic harmonic wavelets were used as the basis functions in the collocation method. The efficiency of our approach, which is connected to the choice of the basis functions, is presented on the testing examples and compared with other methods. It is proved that circular harmonic wavelets satisfy the axioms of the multiresolution analysis.

articleTitle: Absorption and shape transformation of pulse of electromagnetic radiation due to interaction with nanoparticle materials
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: We consider the resonant mechanism of high-frequency radiation absorption by nanoparticles possess either an electrical or a magnetic dipole momentum due to the resonant interaction of electromagnetic radiation with the natural vibration of nanoparticles bounded with carrier by different forces. The frequency range could be varied in wide limits by changing the force constant (e.g. by sintering nanoparticles with the carrier) and by nanoparticle sizes. Shape transformation of pulse of electromagnetic radiation due to reflection from surface is studied. We consider also influence of fluctuations of reflection coefficient on reflected pulse characteristics.

articleTitle: An integral-equation conical solver: some formulas and numerical experiments
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: We present some formulas derived from the developed boundary integral equation theory, which are important for calculations of the efficiency, absorption, and polarization angles of gratings in conical diffraction. Examples of efficiency computations of X-ray grazing-incidence, high-conductive anomalously absorbing, high-spatial-frequency deep transmission, and cross-polarized symmetrical-groove-profiled gratings are considered. The solver tested has been found universal and accurate for calculating various off-plane diffraction problems.

articleTitle: Radiation of a charge passing from vacuum into the left-handed medium
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: We analyse the problem with a charge intersecting the interface between ordinary medium and “left-handed” one. Both the case of semi-infinite media and the case of a cylindrical waveguide are considered. We describe exact and asymptotic approaches for investigation of the electromagnetic field. We note features of spatial radiation due to unusual properties of “left-handed” medium. In particular, the effect of “reversed Cherenkov-transition radiation” (RCTR) is demonstrated both analytically and numerically.

articleTitle: Transient waves in dispersive media: a case of moving planar sources with Gaussian transverse distribution
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: Solutions for the inhomogeneous telegraph equation formed by the Gaussian transverse sources are constructed. Relations describing the transient waves are obtained. Interpretation of these wavefunctions and analytical results for some important cases are discussed.

articleTitle: Metrological aspects of computer based measurement systems in radionavigating complexes
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: The paper concerns estimation of correctness of detection, recognition and treatment of real signals in specialized computing devices. The classical approach to recognition of signals is complemented by construction of probabilistic space of machine analogues. Also, a technique of application of specialized computing devices to problems of certification of hardware-software decisions is described.

articleTitle: 2-D nonlinear Schroedinger equation. Numerical aspects
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: Various numerical methods are employed in order to approximate 2-D nonlinear Schroedinger equation, namely: (i) the classical explicit method, (ii) the Crank-Nicolson implicit scheme, (iii) the Hardin-Tappert split step Fourier method, (iv) the operator exponential scheme, (v) the simplified operator exponential scheme. A comparison between these schemes is made. The approach for comparison is to (a) fix the accuracy; (b) leave mesh parameters (Δx,Δy,Δt) free and compare the computing time required to attain such accuracy for various choices of the parameters. The results of our study suggest operator exponential schemes as the most effective numerical schemes for 2-D nonlinear Shroedinger equation.

articleTitle: Wave speed-porosity scaling for cellular solids
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: We present general arguments for the dependence of wave speed upon the porosity of cellular solids. In particular, we explore this relationship in the context of the topology of the network architecture. We show that the wave speed in cellular solids having rigid network topology equals 0.58 times the speed in the porosity filled continuum made of the same material. This is a very universal result which is independent of the material properties and is valid asymptotically in the long wavelength and thin cell wall limits. This scaling is shown to be linear with volume fraction for mechanism topologies in a high porosity medium. We further show that a scaling law with a single exponent violates the Hashin-Shtrikhman bounds, hence untenable. The advantage of stiffness for kinematically rigid networks over mechanism topology networks disappears for a volume fraction of about 0.56. An extended version of this work will be published elsewhere.

articleTitle: Instability of the electromagnetic surface waves supported by the plasma column
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: A study is made of the linear stage of parametric instability of electromagnetic waves guided by anisotropic cylinder surrounded by uniform dielectric space. A three wave interaction can occur if the space-time condition between the external electric field and the guided waves takes place. The expression of instability increment of guided whistler waves is obtained. For the some practically interesting cases numerical analyses have been performed.

articleTitle: Undistorted progressive waves resulting from separation of variables in some orthogonal curvilinear coordinate systems
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: New families of waves, solutions of the homogeneous wave equation akin to Bateman-Hillion relatively undistorted progressive waves and focus wave modes, where constructed on the basis of separation of variables in the wave equation and specific Bateman transformations in the circular cylindrical, elliptic cylindrical, and parabolic cylindrical coordinate systems.

articleTitle: Separable-variable solutions of the wave equation from a general type of solutions of paraxial wave equation
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: New separable-variable solutions of the 3D scalar wave equation are suggested on the basis of recently introduced new solutions of the 1D paraxial wave equation.

articleTitle: Asymptotics of resonances for curved coupled waveguides
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: A system of two curved quantum waveguides laterally coupled through a small window is considered by solving a boundary value problem with the Dirichlet conditions at the external boundaries and the Neumann conditions at an interface with the window. Asymptotic expansions (with respect to the window size) for a resonance induced by the window and for a bound state induced by the waveguide curvature are obtained using the method of matching of the asymptotic expansions of solutions of the boundary-value problem.

articleTitle: Account of resonance relaxation in the framework of double phase continuum mechanics
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: The report is devoted to consistent description of sound propagation in a double phase fluid taking into account resonance properties of such medium. The approach is based on the generalized variational principle for dissipative hydrodynamics and it gives the description of resonance behavior of liquid with air bubbles in terms of continuum mechanics of double phases medium.

articleTitle: Counting eigenvalues of Schrödinger operator with δ-potential supported by loop
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: The Schrödinger operator with an attractive δ-potential supported by a loop is considered. For such an operator we estimate the number of negative eigenvalues from below and from above in terms of geometrical properties of the support of δ-potential.

articleTitle: The Z(c, n) numbers and their application in the theory of waveguides
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: The positive real numbers Z(c,n) are defined for c - arbitrary, real and n = 1, 2, 3, ... The cases c - diferent from zero or a negative integer, c - zero or an even negative integer and c - an odd negative integer, are considered. If a = c/2 - jk - complex, c - real, (c ≠ l, l = 0,-1,-2, ...), k - real, x = jz, z - real, positive and n = 1, 2, 3, ..., Z(c,n) numbers are called the positive purely imaginary zeros ζ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(c)</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k,n</sub> in x of the complex Kummer confluent hypergeometric function Φ(a, c; x), on condition that k = 0. A theorem is formulated and proved numerically that extends the definition of numbers also for c = l in which Φ(a, c; x) has simple poles and reveals some of their properties. It is composed of three lemmas. Lemmas 1 and 2 substantiate the existence of quantities and determine them when l = 2p, p = 0,-1,-2, ... (l = 0,-2,-4, ..., c - zero or an even negative integer) and l = 2p - 1 (l = -1,-3,-5, ..., c - an odd negative integer), as the common limits of the couples of infinite sequences of positive real numbers {Z(l - ε,n)} and {Z(l+ε,n)}, and {Z(l-ε,n)} and {Z(l+ε,n+1)}), resp. for ε → 0 (ε - infinitesimal positive real number). Lemma 3 demonstrates the possibility to express the numbers Z(l,n), (l - an odd negative integer) through the ones Z(2-l,n), (the symmetry of both quantities with respect to the point c = 1) and presents the relation of Z(0,n) and Z(2,n) with the Ludolphian number π. Tables and graphs visualize the effect of parameters c and n on Z(c,n). The role of the latter is shown in the theory of azimuthally magnetized circular ferrite waveguides that support normal TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0n</sub> modes.

articleTitle: Algebraic aspects of multidimensional δ-shocks and singularities of flux-functions
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: The algebraic aspects of δ-shock wave type solutions to multidimensional systems of conservation laws are studied. We show that any singular solution of the Cauchy problem generates some algebraic relations between its distributional components (“right” singular superpositions of distributions). We prove that the nonlinear flux-functions for δ-shock solutions are well defined Schwartz distributions, and describe their singularities.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

articleTitle: 80 years to professor V. S. Buldyrev
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: This year we celebrated the 80-th anniversary of Vladimir Sergeevitch Buldyrev - the eminent scientist in the field of mathematical theory of wave phenomena! The progress in science would be impossible without scientific schools which in its term need “condensation centers”. As an example professor G. I. Petrashen could be nominated as such center in the 50-ies. Later on this role had moved to younger researches among whom was Vladimir Sergeevitch Buldyrev. Vladimir Sergeevitch had been a remarkable organizer of science: more than twenty of his pupils got their doctoral degree and six of them became professors, the initiation of “Diffraction Days” is strongly binded with his name.

articleTitle: Contents
publicationTitle: Proceedings of the International Conference Days on Diffraction 2009
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: electromagnetic wave propagation; physical optics; metamaterials; quantum mechanics; and quantum optics.
